Subject: Defense control & evidence request — Novapulse MSA/Order Form

Hi Asha / Tom,

Thanks again for the conversation this week. Attached are our proposed redlines for the MSA and the Order Form (PDF/Word). Key points we want to resolve in this round:

- Defense & control for third-party IP claims: our standard is to accept 'defend and control' for third-party infringement claims where the claim arises from our service as delivered, with standard cooperation/notice obligations.
- Carveouts: we do not defend claims arising solely from Customer-provided content, Customer fine-tuning, or open-source components where Customer has accepted open-source obligations.
- Evidence / incident artifacts: Novapulse asked for a way to verify prompt provenance and incident timelines — we've attached a technical-evidence-checklist that explains what we can provide operationally (logs, request IDs, sample payloads, redacted transcripts).

Requested next steps:
1) Please confirm whether Novapulse can accept the carveouts above or propose narrow alternative language.
2) If you need additional evidence (e.g., signed SOC report, sample redacted transcript), tell us which items to prepare from the attached checklist and we will start the evidence collection process.
3) If procurement is comfortable, we'll prepare a DocuSign envelope for the Order Form once language is agreed.

Attachments: Novapulse_MSA_redline.pdf; OrderForm_Novapulse_redline.docx; technical-evidence-checklist.pdf

Thanks,

Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Contracts & Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Defense control & evidence request — Novapulse MSA/Order Form

Stephanie —

Thanks for the redlines and checklist. A few initial items from Legal/Procurement:

1) Defense & control: Novapulse is generally ok with Redwood defending and controlling third-party IP suits, but we need explicit language that (a) Redwood will not settle in a way that imposes ongoing obligations on Novapulse without our consent, and (b) Redwood will indemnify for attorney fees and damages resulting from an affirmative finding of infringement.

2) Carveouts: the open-source carveout is acceptable provided Redwood confirms the specific OSS licenses excluded (we can't accept broad 'open-source' without a list).

3) Evidence: procurement asks for the following before final signature — a current SOC 2 Type II report, a sample redacted transcript for a production request showing request ID and redaction, and the technical-evidence-checklist filled out with expected turnaround times for each item.

4) Cap: our commercial team will push back if the indemnity cap is 1x fees. We need to understand Redwood's comfort with a higher limit or an insurance-first solution.

Please see our in-line comments on the attached Order Form (I'll send separately). We want to keep the timeline to signature within two weeks if we can align on evidence and cap approach.

Thanks,

Asha Reddy
Senior Counsel, Novapulse
asha.reddy@novapulse.com

Hi Asha / Tom —

Appreciate the quick read. Short answers and concrete proposals below so procurement/legal can decide quickly:

1) Settlements: we can add express language that Redwood will not enter a settlement that imposes ongoing performance obligations or monetary obligations on Novapulse without prior written consent. We will cover reasonable attorneys' fees and any damages awarded in a final judgment or settlement that Redwood enters to resolve the claim.

2) OSS carveout: fair — can you provide the vendor list or OSS components you expect us to exclude? In the absence of a list, we suggest a limited OSS carveout that only excludes software where Novapulse (a) incorporated the OSS into its product and (b) accepted the OSS license terms directly.

3) Evidence & SOC: SOC 2 Type II is an internal document with confidentiality controls; we can provide a bridge letter summarizing scope and last audit date and share the SOC under NDA/appropriate handling instructions. For the sample redacted transcript and request ID mapping, see the attached technical-evidence-checklist — we can deliver the items marked 'available' within 10 business days after signature and the rest within 20 business days.

4) Cap / Insurance-first path: Marcus and I propose an insurance-first approach — Redwood maintains a $5M policy and we agree that indemnity will be subject to the policy limits as primary for third-party IP claims; if policy proceeds are insufficient, Redwood's backstop will be limited to $2M. We are open to discussion around a higher combined cap but prefer an insurance-first solution to avoid material balance sheet exposure.

If that approach sounds reasonable, we'll update the Order Form and send a DocuSign envelope for signature.

Attachments: technical-evidence-checklist.pdf (updated with estimated turnaround times)

Best,

Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Contracts & Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

Internal note (Novapulse not on this reply) —

Quick thoughts to shape our next draft:

- Insurance-first approach is marketable; $5M primary policy + $2M Redwood backstop should be acceptable for a mid-market customer like Novapulse. Keep settlement protections (no consent-free settlements imposing obligations on the customer).
- For OSS carveout: propose a two-week window post-signature for Novapulse to provide an OSS list. If they don't, default to our limited-carveout language (only OSS incorporated & accepted by Customer license).
- Evidence delivery: confirm we can redact customer content and provide request IDs with a hashed mapping for provenance; that prevents exposing other customers.

I'll draft the redline language for the insurance-first cap and the OSS list timeline and send to Camila/Stephanie by EOD.

—Marcus
